1. Dataset Description
The dataset I will be using is William Shakespeare's 'Hamlet', edited by Charles Kean (Project gutenberg,1859). It is approximately 30,000 words snd consists of 17th century English but I am working with a republished and edited verion from the 19th century so their may be lingusitic variation in the text from the time period change. 
I found this text on project gutenberg because I knew I wanted to use Hamlet and figured this was the easiest way to get a copy. Link: https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/27761/pg27761.txt
The format is already in plain text so I won't have to make adaptions to it thankfully. This is the other reason I used gutenberg

2. Rationale
I choose this dataset because I love the play Hamlet and I am fasinated with many diffrent aspects and many diffrent characters within the play. For this project, I am specifically focuesd on whether Shakespeare specific linguistic choices are a reflection of narrative intention or are merely a biproduct of place and cohesion. More simply, did shakespeare have narrative intention for his lingustic choices or did they just sound good? I can see it going either way honestly
3. Type of Analysis
I will most likely be using the Frequency & vocablulary section to analyze sentence structure and word choice to determine if a sentence is passive or active. I will be counting sentences for this project. Maybe closer to paragraphs it will depend on how sentences interact with one another.
